cluster.label: Childhood NCLs: vision loss + seizures + regression
cluster.summary: Batten-type diseases that share the core symptom triad of vision loss, seizures and loss of skills.

members.label: CLN5 disease
members.summary: A very rare inherited childhood brain disease that causes vision loss, seizures and loss of skills. There is no approved treatment yet.

members.label: CLN6 disease
members.summary: A rare inherited brain disease of childhood with seizures, vision loss and loss of movement and speech skills.

members.label: CLN2 disease
members.summary: A form of Batten disease that starts in toddlers with seizures and loss of skills. An enzyme replacement therapy is approved.

members.label: CLN3 disease
members.summary: The most common form of Batten disease. It usually starts at school age with vision loss, followed by seizures and loss of skills.

members.label: MOCK ultra-rare NCL subtype X (fictional)
members.summary: A FICTIONAL, made-up ultra-rare Batten-like disease used to demo the 'no known group' case. Not a real diagnosis.

top_phenotypes.label: Seizure
top_phenotypes.summary: Sudden bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain (fits).

top_phenotypes.label: Developmental regression
top_phenotypes.summary: Losing skills (speech, walking, learning) that a child had already gained.

top_mechanisms.label: Lysosomal degradation (ceroid lipofuscin storage)
top_mechanisms.summary: Cells break down worn-out parts inside lysosomes. In all NCLs this recycling fails and waste (lipofuscin) builds up, especially in nerve cells.
